title: What If You Could See Ultraviolet Light? Some People Can
subject: human eye

scenes.text: What if you could see ultraviolet light? Some people can, and it comes with a catch.
Your eye's lens blocks most light below 380 nanometers. That's where ultraviolet begins.
Your retina can sense some of it. The lens is the filter, not the retina.
People who've had a lens removed without a replacement can often see ultraviolet.
Claude Monet had cataract surgery on one eye in 1923. His water lilies turned blue and purple.
Bees, birds and some fish see ultraviolet every day. For them, flowers glow with hidden patterns.
